summary:
The fix is correct. It fixes the right cause and is not looser than the old check except on the release transient, which lets in no byte. My file:line checks are in the notes, K1 to K11.

- **Every write, both ends.** The held bytes grow only at delay.rs:829 (up, move_up) and :1597 (down, poll_write). Each growth is followed, under the same lock, by model_write (:830, :1615), and model_write now ends with check_held_bound(dir) (:634-635). No held-bytes sample runs in between. P1 (down) and P5 (up) both fail at delay_tests.rs:782, so both ends are shown to bite.
- **Same formula.** The check's body (:539-550) is the old loop body word for word. At a down write it reads the same values the old check read at poll_write's sample (:1617). On the up side the old check never sampled at a write, so the new one covers more there.
- **check_held_falls is sound.** Held shrinks only at :1526 and :1771 and grows only at the two sites above. The scanner's buffer is outside the up count. Conn starts empty. The one test that touches the bytes (delay_tests.rs:1796) flips a byte without changing the length. So the held bytes cannot legitimately rise between writes in either direction.
- **No assert got weaker.** The largest-excess figure is now kept only at writes (:549-550). Because G-NC2 asserts held_grew == [0, 0] first (:2313, before :2314), its excess assert is just as strict.
- **Non-test code unchanged.** Every changed non-doc line is a cfg(test) item or statement, or sits in the cfg(test) test module. E5 (the lab binary's hash unchanged) agrees.
- **Difference-set argument (C9).** I derived it myself and it matches the advisor's C6b. Between writes the acknowledged prefix of the same front record can only grow. It falls only when a release moves past the front record (:698-709). So any sample the old check flagged and the new pair passes needs a release since the latest write. Nothing is admitted between writes.
- **Evidence.** The logs bear out build.md:
  - L1 run 94: G-NC2 alone failed with [1, 0]; the diagnostic counters read over_waiting [1, 0] and over_at_write [0, 0].
  - E3a 600 of 600, E3b 600 of 600, E3c 20 of 20, all on the final diff a7199f7a.
  - Light pre-check PASS.
  - P1 to P5 fail on the named lines with the stated values.
  - The current file hashes equal the fixed ones.
- **Doc texts.** They match the design notes word for word and are accurate, apart from the Lows below.
- **Remaining steps.** The plan for them is right. The 552 / 632 pass bar holds because no test was added (e3c shows 169 tests, as L1 did). Free disk is 4,953 MiB, above the floor.

The one Medium is that C9 is not met yet. The argument is not in the plan's "Not looser" line or in build.md, and the report has not been written.

findings.where: .checkpoints/netcode-proof-test/u3c-held-1/u3c-held-1-plan-draft.md:128-129 (sha256 still a53b2803..., its only commit ec70096); .checkpoints/netcode-proof-test/u3c-held-1/build.md (no difference-set text); advisor-plan-review-full.json C9
findings.what: C9 is not met yet. The plan's 'Not looser' line still gives only its three original reasons. build.md has no difference-set argument. C9's two other plan corrections (cite the card entry by name; fix the saver sentence) are not made either. The argument exists only in the advisor's notes (C6b) and in my review notes (K8). There is also a risk for the report: E3's 1,220 passes show only that the new pair of checks raises no false positive. They cannot show the old false positive is gone. E3a's G-NC2-alone mode was never run on HEAD, so its failure rate there is unknown, and e3c's 20 whole-binary runs would catch a 1-in-100 failure only about 18 % of the time.
findings.fix:
Before the advisor's head check, write the argument into the plan's line (as a dated note) and into the report, with code cites:
- Between writes una only rises, so for the same front record the prefix (delay.rs:541-545) never falls.
- Takes (:1530-1534, :1782-1785) leave the front unreleased record unchanged.
- The prefix falls only when harvest moves released[d] past the front record (:698-709).
- So a sample the old check flagged and the new pair passes satisfies held(s) <= held(w) <= B + p(w) and held(s) > B + p(s), which needs p(s) < p(w), which needs a release since the latest write w.
- No byte is admitted between writes (growth only at :829 and :1597, each checked at :635).
- So the fix is looser only on the release transient, and every sample stays below 64 KB + 16,406 B.
Also make the two other C9 plan corrections. In the report, rest 'the flake is gone' on this argument plus L1's diagnostic counters, never on E3's pass counts.

findings.where: .gate/u3c-held-1/p1.log (G-NC2 at delay_tests.rs:2308, left [1, 0], 'writes above the bound [1, 0]'); build.md P1 entry; netcode-architect-design.md F15 and section 3 P1 (b)
findings.what: Under P1, G-NC2 failed at '...at every write' with [1, 0], although the design notes' F15 (my own) predicted a pass ('S drains at once; its ack comes a one-way delay later'). C3 accepts this as evidence, but build.md does not say why the prediction was wrong. My likely explanation, from reading the code and not proven: a record released after a loss inside it carries its already-acknowledged prefix into the released-but-untaken state. When the writer's own poll_write step (current(), By::App) releases that record in the same step as acks that freed room, the planted down_free admits a write before the pump takes the record. Held then reaches about 64 KB + p against a bound of 64 KB + 0. That is the same window as the original false positive.
findings.fix: Add one line to build.md and the report giving this cause, marked as a reading. Never repeat F15's 'G-NC2 cannot show P1'. Record G-NC2 as a second, probabilistic witness for P1; the stalled-client test stays the deterministic one.

findings.where: delay_tests.rs:787 and :2313 (assert message 'held only falls between writes'); delay_tests.rs:2267-2268 (G-NC2 doc); delay.rs:558-564 (check_held_falls)
findings.what: The message and the G-NC2 doc say the held bytes 'only fall' between writes. check_held_falls checks something weaker: no sample is above what the latest write left. A growth after a drain that stays below held_at_write would not be counted. That is harmless for the bound, because the next write's check sees it, and the code has no such growth anyway (drains only at :1526 and :1771). check_held_falls's own doc (:554-556) states exactly what it checks.
findings.fix: Optional: word the message as what is checked, e.g. 'held never above the latest write's, between writes'. Or keep it, and say in the report that 'only falls' is the code reading and the counter checks its consequence for the bound. This Low does not trigger a push on its own.

findings.where: marks/SERIES.md:613 and :642 (up part); .checkpoints/netcode-proof-test/u3c-plan.md Up line (:126-128); delay.rs:51-52 (module doc, up sentence); delay.rs:375 (Life doc); delay.rs:528 (check_held_bound doc)
findings.what:
Three precision gaps in the new doc texts:
- (a) The SERIES rows' up part, u3c-plan's Up line and the module doc's up sentence say 'at most, at each write, ...'. Unlike the down part, they say nothing about a reading at the second's end, which falls between writes and is what the row reports.
- (b) Life's doc says 'the largest excess of the records held over the 64 KB budget', but that figure is now kept only at writes (:549-550). It equals the overall largest only while held_grew is 0.
- (c) check_held_bound's doc says '(model_write, the only place they grow)'. The bytes actually grow in model_write's two callers just before it (:829, :1597); model_write's doc says so.
findings.fix: (a) Add 'the records only falling between writes' to the up part in the SERIES rows, the plan line and the module doc. (b) Write 'at a write' in Life's doc. (c) Optional nit: '(at model_write, right after its caller adds the record's bytes)'. None of these triggers a push on its own; fold them into the fix pass if one happens, otherwise record them as a follow-up.
